# Reproducing FloodScan {#sec-floodscan-repro}

---
jupyter: ds-flood-gfm
---

The goal is an open flooded-fraction product. FloodScan (AER's AFED) is the
benchmark the team already licenses, and its algorithm is published in AER's
Algorithm Description Document, so the sanity check is to rebuild it from
public data and see how close we get. The reproduction itself is not for
publication; a product derived from FloodScan would need AER's approval. What
we learn from it is which stages carry the skill, and that transfers to a
product calibrated on the team's own validation maps.

The long-form record is `docs/floodscan-algorithm-notes.md`. Every table in
this chapter is loaded from a committed result file under
`results/floodscan_repro/`, regenerated and diffed against the code on
2026-11-27 (`experiments/floodscan_repro/diagnostics/regen_results.sh`). The
scripts behind each section are listed in
`experiments/floodscan_repro/diagnostics/README.md`.

```{python}
#| code-summary: "load the committed result tables (fails loudly if they are missing)"
from pathlib import Path
import pandas as pd

RES = next((p for p in (Path("results/floodscan_repro"), Path("../results/floodscan_repro")) if p.exists()), None)
if RES is None:
    raise FileNotFoundError("results/floodscan_repro not found; run from the repo or book_gfm directory")


def table(rel, cols=None, index="variant"):
    df = pd.read_csv(RES / rel)
    if cols:
        df = df[[index] + cols]
    return df.set_index(index)


pd.options.display.float_format = "{:.2f}".format
```

## AER's chain, and how much of it we built

AER's retrieval works on 37 GHz passive-microwave brightness temperatures.
The polarisation ratio PRI = (V − H)/(V + H) rises with open water; a
transform Q of it is linear in the flooded fraction. The rest of the chain is
about deciding what "dry" looks like at each pixel and day, rejecting rain,
and filtering noise. Our implementation runs on NOAA's 0.25° daily AMSR2
grids over a West Africa box (0–20°E, 0–20°N) and uses two training years to
build the reference tables that AER builds from more than ten.

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-cap: "The FloodScan (AFED) chain as described by AER, and our status per stage. Green = built and scored; amber = built on the coarse grid, with a known limitation; red = not possible on our data yet."
flowchart TD
  A["AMSR2 Tb 36/18/23/89 GHz<br/>NOAA CSU 0.25° daily grid<br/>(AER: 5′ footprint matching)"]:::amber
  B["PRI → Q<br/>atmospheric correction (MERRA-2)"]:::done
  C["rain flags<br/>scattering index, snow, desert tests<br/>+ 2-cell dilation"]:::done
  D["dry reference Q_dry<br/>climatology Qdc blended with<br/>61-day in-season expectation"]:::amber
  E["flooded fraction<br/>eq. 13 mixing with open-water Q_pow"]:::done
  F["noise floor MDFF<br/>3σ of 7-day variance<br/>+ coastal rule"]:::amber
  G["f_hop: kurtosis of day-to-day change<br/>3-day weights, outlier half-weight"]:::done
  H["spatial merge (eq. 18)<br/>fill-in decay, flash filter"]:::done
  I["output: SFED daily<br/>1/12° (AER's 90 m step not attempted)"]:::amber
  A --> B --> C --> D --> E --> F --> G --> H --> I
  classDef done fill:#cfe8cf,stroke:#2e7d32;
  classDef amber fill:#ffe9b3,stroke:#b26a00;
  classDef blocked fill:#f8c9c9,stroke:#c62828;
```

| stage (AER ADD section) | ours | limitation |
|---|---|---|
| input grid | NOAA CSU 0.25° daily, 2023–2025 (only years the grid product covers) | AER matches 22 km footprints onto a 5′ grid; our grid carries about twice the day-to-day noise |
| PRI, Q, atmospheric correction | built; correction is neutral at these latitudes | |
| rain flags | built (Ferraro 1996 with AER's changes); the single largest gain | |
| dry reference | climatology from two years, blended with the in-season expectation | two years cannot absorb inter-annual surface variation (see the hold-out) |
| flooded fraction, MDFF, f_hop, 3-day weights | built, filter windows rescaled from 5′ to 0.25° | |
| spatial merge, fill-in, flash filter | built; the merge fires but does not change scores at 0.25° | |
| 90 m downscaling | not attempted; @sec-downscaling-poc covers the prior-based route | |

## Scores against FloodScan, West Africa, August–November 2024

Reference tables from 2023 and 2025, test year 2024, scored cell by cell
against FloodScan SFED resampled to the same grid. The metrics: `ratio` is
our total flooding divided by FloodScan's; `never` is the share of our
flooded cell-days in cells FloodScan never floods that season; `r_cell`,
`r_blk` are per-cell and 0.5° block correlations of the daily series;
`r_lga1` is the median per-LGA correlation; `peak` is our seasonal peak
divided by FloodScan's at the LGA level; `lag` is the median timing offset
in days. Each variant switches one stage off.

```{python}
#| code-summary: "2024 variant table, whole box"
table("nga2024_variant_summary.csv", ["ratio", "never", "r_cell", "r_blk", "r_lga1", "r_lga2", "peak", "peak_mm", "lag"])
```

```{python}
#| code-summary: "2024, inland cells only"
table("nga2024_variant_summary_inland.csv")
```

Reading the 2024 run: inland, we produce the right amount of flooding
(ratio 0.92) with little in the wrong place (12% never-flooded), and the
daily series correlate at 0.70 per cell and 0.82 per block. The rain flags
carry most of the gain (`norain`). The coast is over-flooded in every variant
(whole-box `never` 0.41 against inland 0.12). Peaks come in low (about half
of FloodScan's at LGA level) and a parameter sweep found no knob that fixes
them without inflating the total; a two-week test showed the 0.25° grid has
about twice the 7-day noise of footprint matching, which is where the
noise floor comes from.

## The hold-out: swapping the years

Every score above tested 2024 with tables from 2023 and 2025. Swapping roles
(tables from 2024 and 2025, test year 2023) asks whether the method or the
year was doing the work.

```{python}
#| code-summary: "2023 hold-out variant table"
table("holdout_2023/nga2023_variant_summary.csv", ["ratio", "never", "r_cell", "r_blk", "r_lga1", "peak", "peak_mm", "lag"])
```

It failed: nearly five times FloodScan's total, four fifths of it where
FloodScan never floods, per-cell correlation 0.39. The diagnosis
(`q_level_by_year.py`, `sahel_tables_diag.py`):

```{python}
#| code-summary: "yearly land medians of Q and 18 GHz Tb: no calibration step between years"
q = pd.read_csv(RES / "holdout_2023/q_level_by_year.csv")
q[q.variable.isin(["Q_36_asc", "Tb_18v_asc"])].pivot(index=["variable", "month"], columns="year", values="median")
```

The satellite data agree across years to the third decimal, so it is not
calibration. The excess sits in the Sahel band (12.5–17.5°N) in
October–November:

```{python}
#| code-summary: "Sahel-band Q cycle by year, 36 GHz ascending, 10-day blocks"
#| fig-cap: "Median Q over land in the Sahel band (12.5–17.5°N, solid) and south of it (dashed), by 10-day block from 1 June. The band's dry-down in late 2023 reaches 0.365–0.367; 2024 and 2025 stop at 0.356–0.362. South of 12.5°N the three years are indistinguishable."
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

c = pd.read_csv(RES / "holdout_2023/sahel_band_q_cycle.csv")
c["doy"] = pd.to_datetime(c.block_start).dt.dayofyear
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4))
for (year, region), g in c.groupby(["year", "region"]):
    ax.plot(g.doy, g.median_Q_36_asc, ls="-" if region.startswith("band") else "--",
            color={2023: "tab:red", 2024: "tab:blue", 2025: "tab:green"}[year],
            label=f"{year} {'Sahel band' if region.startswith('band') else 'south'}")
ax.set_xlabel("day of year (10-day blocks from 1 June)"); ax.set_ylabel("median Q (36 GHz, asc)")
ax.legend(ncol=3, fontsize=8); ax.grid(alpha=0.3)
plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| code-summary: "the dry references the two table sets give the band, mid-season dates"
r = pd.read_csv(RES / "holdout_2023/sahel_band_references.csv")
pd.options.display.float_format = "{:.4f}".format
r[r.table.isin(["Qdc_36_asc", "MDFF_36_asc"])].pivot(index=["table", "date"], columns="training_years", values=["band_12.5_17.5N", "south_of_12.5N"])
```

In the Sahel the 36 GHz signal has a soil and vegetation cycle that is not
water: it dips in the rains and climbs through the dry-down. Late 2023 climbed
about 0.005 higher than 2024 and 2025. The two-year climatology built from
those years sits below it by that amount, which the mixing equation turns into
a flooded fraction of about 0.09, right where the band's noise floor
(0.10–0.11) sits. South of 12.5°N the year-to-year spread is below 0.001,
so the Nigeria scores stand; the 2024 result looked clean partly because
2024's dry-down happened to fall inside the 2023 and 2025 range. The coastal
states (Lagos, Rivers, Bayelsa, Akwa Ibom) are over-flooded ten to fifty
times in both years, a standing defect the inland 2024 floods hid.

Giving the in-season expectation real weight (AER's blend gives the
climatology 99.9% of the weight when it comes from two years) halves the
false total but does not restore skill, and erodes 2024, because a 61-day
median absorbs real slow floods too:

```{python}
#| code-summary: "expectation-weight test, both years"
pd.options.display.float_format = "{:.2f}".format
rows = []
for year in (2023, 2024):
    for w in ("1e5", "1e6", "1e7"):
        s = pd.read_csv(RES / f"wexp/{year}_{w}/nga{year}_variant_summary.csv").iloc[0]
        rows.append({"test year": year, "w_exp": w, "ratio": s.ratio, "never": s.never, "r_cell": s.r_cell, "r_lga1": s.r_lga1, "peak": s.peak})
pd.DataFrame(rows).set_index(["test year", "w_exp"])
```

## Where we are, and the open decision

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-cap: "Status of the FloodScan reproduction, November 2026, and the decision tree in front of us."
flowchart TD
  A["chain built end to end<br/>on the 0.25° grid"]:::done
  B["2024 test: inland on target,<br/>peaks half, coast over-flooded"]:::amber
  C["2023 hold-out failed:<br/>two-year dry reference<br/>cannot absorb Sahel variation"]:::blocked
  D["36 GHz swaths 2019–2022,<br/>aggregated to 0.25°<br/>~10 GB per season, ~40 GB"]:::todo
  E["rebuild tables from 5–6 years<br/>with AER's per-day level regression;<br/>repeat the hold-out"]:::todo
  F{"Sahel false alarms gone?"}
  G["full swath route:<br/>5′ grid, all channels,<br/>10+ seasons ≈ 250–325 GB streamed"]:::todo
  H["the problem is elsewhere;<br/>250 GB saved"]:::todo
  A --> B --> C --> D --> E --> F
  F -- yes --> G
  F -- no --> H
  classDef done fill:#cfe8cf,stroke:#2e7d32;
  classDef amber fill:#ffe9b3,stroke:#b26a00;
  classDef blocked fill:#f8c9c9,stroke:#c62828;
  classDef todo fill:#ffffff,stroke:#9e9e9e,stroke-dasharray: 4 3;
```

What is settled: the chain is implemented stage by stage as AER describes
it, the rain flags are the stage that matters most, inland Nigeria is
reproduced to within 10% in amount and 0.7 in daily correlation for one
year, and the coarse grid and the two-year reference are the two things
standing between that and "close to perfect". What is not settled is whether
a long record fixes the reference: a longer mean may not cover a genuinely
high dry-down year, and what more years really enable is a realistic spread
estimate and AER's per-day level regression, which two years cannot support.
The cheapest discriminating step is the 40 GB test in the figure; it needs a
go-ahead because of the transfer volume.

Everything the chapter rests on is preserved: the branch is on GitHub, the
input grids, reference tables and flooded-fraction files are on the team's
dev blob with a sha256 manifest (`experiments/backup_rebuild_data.py`), and
the result tables are committed and regenerate byte for byte.
